EUR-USD - Another example:

Let's take a closer look at what happens on the LTF:

HTF First (15M Chart)

On the 1-minute chart it is easy to see how price is reacting to a LTF true supply zone. Price returns to the MPL of this zone to consume FOF. Price proceeds to compress all the way down to the last set of orders...which is exactly where price reacted on its FTB.

author: hoeschec
text:
EUR-JPY - New example...this time one that failed.

Here is the 15M chart:

Here is the LTF 1-min chart:

I would have went short at FL Box A, since FL Box B reacted off of it. I would have chose a higher level (earlier EG) but I saw no areas with FOF...it was all spiked. The solid red lines shows where price reacted.

Not every setup works, which is why I must remember to always control risk and only choose the highest R:R opportunities.

One last look at the area where price bounced....good area, but I wouldn't have traded it because I saw OF was already spiked/consumed. Obviously there was enough still left over...

author: hoeschec
text:
More examples: USD -CAD

This zone was a great area to get long....1-min chart provided the perfect entry. All LTF swap zones drawn, and price bounced as expected.

Start with a higher time frame chart to find a good swap zone, then check LTF to ID all smaller swap zones to refine entry. Refined entry = small stop = high R:R

Entry point shown on chart below..amazing how well price bounced at this level!

text:
This is getting fun

Another perfect example USD-CAD:

Higher time frame:

LTF- look for lower time frame swap zones. In this scenario there are two swap zones that look like they could both work. Please refer to the chart below. Within FL Box D you can see FL Box A & B - both are good swap zones.

Look at the red circle...you will see there is a tiny swap zone there...it is also an important DP. Price will bounce at or near to this level.

And the trade result...perfect reaction.

author: hoeschec
text:
USD-JPY - tough FO on this...this FO broke the low of FL Box 1, which is the lowest level I can see as a possible origin/true demand. FL Box 2 looks like a reaction to FL Box 1.

Any ideas on a way to avoid something like this? The engulf was valid, and price hit its target, but the nasty fakeout would have stopped me out.

author: hoeschec

AUD-USD

Hourly (HTF) Chart:

1-minute chart shows the swap zone that formed. Price bounced right at this zone.

author: hoeschec
text:
AUD-USD

HTF shows price FO to MPL...but no EG to the upside.

This is a good location to look for a TT when price RT.

HTF:

LTF Swap Zones shown: Fl Box D could also be a good place to short, but when in doubt, choose the most recent swap zone with FOF still existing. In this case, Fl Box C ended up being the location where price bounced.

There is an especially strong bounce, with a substantial downside follow-through (over 400 pip drop proceeding the reaction to this FL). This is somewhat predictable considering price FO to a HTF MPL without engulfing to the upside.

USD-CHF - there was a HTF opportunity to short this (as you can see on the Daily chart below) but I am focusing on the LTF opportunity to buy.

Daily chart shows price bounce at an important HTF supply zone, but there was no EG to the upside. Because of this, I want to be cautious taking any longs, as price may RT quite far. Still, there is a good place with FOF where a scalp is possible.

The hourly chart zooms in on the location:

LTF shows the swap zones and entry.

Quick scalp, conservative target.
